text: Automated retraining for a production Amazon Bedrock classifier that rates research documents by importance: on an EventBridge schedule a larger LLM grades its ratings, and fine-tuning runs only when the grades shift past a threshold
decisive_wording: B: "using a larger LLM as a judge on an EventBridge schedule and fine-tuning only when its scores move past a threshold" vs A: "a larger LLM grades its ratings ... when the grades shift past a threshold" vs C: "Built LLM-as-a-judge gating for a production Amazon Bedrock document-importance classifier"
info: A and B keep the same facts: automated retraining, production Bedrock classifier, research documents rated by importance, larger LLM evaluating on an EventBridge schedule, threshold-gated fine-tuning. B also names the recognized 'LLM as a judge' pattern in plain phrasing. C adds an action verb ('Built') and the judge term, but drops 'research documents' (compressed to 'document-importance') and the explicit 'automated retraining' framing, and 'scores it' leaves unclear what is being scored.
